_comment: Template for your organization's MANAGED settings, deployed by your device-management or server-managed-settings mechanism. Managed settings apply after every other source, so a user cannot override them. This is what makes the AI Engineering OS non-bypassable. Verify every key against the current settings reference before relying on it, and delete the _comment keys before use.
_lock_comment: Without this, an engineer can drop a file at .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md and shadow the plugin's reviewer, or add a project hook that undoes a guard. Blocks skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from user and project sources so they can only come from plugins or managed settings.
_sideload_comment: Rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents and --mcp-config at startup, which are otherwise a one-command bypass of the line above.
_marketplace_comment: Register the organization's marketplace centrally so engineers do not add it by hand, and so the name cannot be claimed by another source.
_enable_comment: Roll the plugin out to everyone rather than asking each engineer to install it.
_permissions_comment: Structural denies. Stronger than the plugin's command guards, because they stop the Read and Write tools directly rather than pattern-matching a shell string. Deny is evaluated before ask and allow, and a deny rule cannot carry allowlist exceptions.
_model_comment: Restricting availableModels changes what the plugin's model policy can resolve to. If opus is not permitted, HIGH and CRITICAL roles are substituted downward and the risk floors in policies/risk-classification.json stop being met, silently. Check the allowlist against the floors before restricting.
_teams_comment: Agent teams are experimental and off by default. Set this deliberately: the plugin works without them, and one stage is TEAM_REQUIRED and escalates rather than silently falling back. See docs/execution.md.
